title: Mayor
statement: Oakland deserves a Council review that starts with the record, not another Ivy Hill headline. INIT-014 is a $2.5 million proposal marked vote-scheduled; it is not funded, and my C116 work request failed without changing that status. Ivy Hill sentiment has improved to 0.01, retail vitality has slipped to 5.05, and four incidents were reported this cycle—mixed evidence, not an emergency script. My fresh work request asks for review of the filed legislation on those facts, with INIT-011 and INIT-013 kept visibly separate. I welcome Warren Ashford’s fiscal scrutiny and Nina Chen’s process questions; overlapping measures must not blur purpose or accountability. Only a passed council vote can fund INIT-014, and I will not announce a vote date the record does not supply.

payload.text: The C117 petition display for C115–C117 reports seven complaints and seven constructive-participation entries; participation is not a response count. Its response section supplies no committed-response or media-outcome receipts, so the current record does not verify the earlier eleven-complaint/seven-response formulation or provide a complaint-by-complaint crosswalk. I am treating that earlier formulation as unverified, not reconciled. On INIT-014, Initiative_Tracker records a proposed, vote-scheduled Ivy Hill Community Support Initiative with $2.5 million remaining and voteCycle null. MV-116-civic-office-mayor-2026-11-16 records: “write failed: row not processed.” That failed work request was not a council vote, funding, or a completed review; a passed council vote remains the funding gate, and no vote date is supplied. On INIT-007, the project record contains no placement-gap analysis and names no office responsible for publishing one. That publishing-office assignment is missing from the supplied records. My office owes the public a named publisher and the document itself before claiming delivery; I will not invent either.
